entry.title: 【Day 5】 Iceland 5-Day Trip
entry.content:
It’s our last day in Iceland~ We joined another day tour, this time heading to South Iceland.

Departure

The weather was especially nice today. We finally got some sunshine! When I booked the tour, I specifically chose today to visit the most beautiful part of South Iceland hehe~

The scenery along the way was absolutely gorgeous! The wisps of white mist rising from the ground were hot steam caused by volcanic activity. It was my first time seeing something like this. Such a fascinating sight!

Saw some very interesting books at a rest stop…

We also saw tons of cows, horses, and baa baa sheep along the way~

Eyjafjallajökull

Although this was not explicitly listed as one of the stops when I booked the tour, we actually passed by Eyjafjallajökull!! Our guide was also super nice and let us get off the bus to take a look~

Eyjafjallajökull is a glacier in southern Iceland and the fifth largest glacier in the country. It is located west of the much larger Mýrdalsjökull ice cap. Beneath the glacier lies a 1666 meter tall volcano, which has erupted frequently since the Ice Age.

Unfortunately, it was covered by clouds, so we could not actually see it. Not the best luck…

Skógafoss

We’re almost at Skógafoss~ It is one of Iceland’s largest and most famous waterfalls, standing 60 meters tall and about 15 meters wide. On sunny days, the mist often catches the sunlight and creates beautiful rainbows, which is why it is known as the Rainbow Waterfall. It is nice and sunny today, so hopefully we will get to see one!

There did not seem to be much of a rainbow from far away, and apparently it depends on your viewing angle. From certain angles, it becomes much more obvious!

You can see that at this distance, there were barely any rocks left above the water to step on. I just barely managed to avoid getting my shoes wet. If you get any closer, the waterfall mist will absolutely soak you, so I highly recommend bringing a waterproof shell jacket to Iceland!

Vík í Mýrdal

Next stop, Vík í Mýrdal~ It is about 180 kilometers from the capital, Reykjavík, and is also the southernmost village in Iceland.

We’ve arrived in Vík~

The church in Vík has that classic Icelandic countryside church style and often appears on scenic postcards. That little splash of red against the blue sky and white clouds somehow gives me Studio Ghibli vibes~

The rock formations in the distance are another famous Icelandic attraction called Reynisdrangar. They are mysterious basalt sea stacks rising from the ocean, reaching up to fifteen meters tall. According to local folklore, Reynisdrangar was formed when three trolls were caught by sunlight and turned to stone. Another legend says they are the remains of a ship with three masts.

Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach

Reynisfjara is famous for its black sand, basalt columns, and the raging waves of the Atlantic Ocean. The sand is black because of the beach’s volcanic origins. During volcanic eruptions, lava flowed into the sea and cooled into solid rock. Over time, powerful waves continuously smashed and eroded the rock into tiny fragments, eventually creating this unique black sand beach.

Tall basalt columns line the cliffs of Reynisfjall Mountain. These hexagonal columns formed naturally as lava cooled~

Next to the basalt columns, Reynisfjara is also home to a cave called Hálsanefshellir. It is famous for its unusual basalt column formations and really shows off nature’s artistic side. The geometric rock patterns were sculpted through a combination of volcanic activity and erosion.

You can actually walk into the cave and get a closer look at the rock columns~

The black sand beach is notorious for its dangerous “sneaker waves,” which have taken many lives. Our guide repeatedly warned us not to get too close to the water and absolutely never to turn our backs on the ocean.

Dyrhólaey is located at Iceland’s southernmost point. In Icelandic, the name Dyrhólaey roughly means “the hill island with the door hole.” It has a gigantic natural sea arch. The huge rock arch at the end of the peninsula was formed by hundreds of years of erosion from ocean waves. It is so massive that boats and even small aircraft have passed directly through it before. Unfortunately, Dyrhólaey was not included in our itinerary today, so we could only admire it from afar.

Sólheimajökull

Sólheimajökull is an outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull on Iceland’s south coast. It is famous for its vivid blue ice and streaks of volcanic ash. Layers of ash left behind by past volcanic eruptions stretch across the glacier’s surface, creating spectacular ridges and patterns.

You can really tell how huge a difference sunshine makes in Iceland compared to cloudy weather, right? qwq

Seljalandsfoss

Seljalandsfoss has a unique little trail that allows you to walk behind the falling water during summer and admire the curtain of water from the back.

Seljalandsfoss is part of the Seljalandsá River, whose water comes from melting snow and ice from Eyjafjallajökull. In 2010, the volcano beneath the ice cap erupted violently, causing major flight disruptions across Europe. Seljalandsfoss itself is relatively narrow, but the water drops straight down from a towering cliff. Several centuries ago, this cliff was actually part of Iceland’s coastline. The coast has since retreated beyond the surrounding lowlands, but you can still see the ocean in the distance from the waterfall.

I was completely soaked after walking the whole loop, but it was SO worth it!!! It really felt like one of those rare experiences you only get a few chances to have in your entire life!!! Once again, I cannot emphasize enough how important a waterproof shell jacket is (

Back to the Hotel

And that wraps up the trip perfectly!!!

Although Reykjavík itself was honestly a little boring, the natural landscapes everywhere else were absolutely breathtaking. I feel like I have to come back someday and do a full road trip around Iceland before my life can truly feel complete!! I’ll definitely be back!!!

As for the food, I really could not get used to it. Everything was expensive and tasted pretty bad. Skyr was basically the only thing that suited my taste. Next time I come, I am definitely bringing loads of instant food, cup noodles, pickles, snacks, and stuff like that (

And the weather is SUPER important here. It really comes down to luck. On cloudy days, the scenery definitely loses quite a bit of its beauty, although the gloomy weather has its own unique charm too. But still, I would much rather have sunshine! I would say I got pretty lucky this time. On my final day, the sky was completely clear without a single cloud!

entry.title: 【Day 4】 Iceland 5-Day Trip
entry.content:
Day 4 was still spent wandering around the capital city~

Höggmyndagarðurinn Sculpture Park

Next to Hallgrímskirkja there is a small park with many sculptures, free to visit. Very quiet, with very few tourists. Beside the garden there is also a paid museum, The Einar Jónsson Museum, which we did not enter. The statues are actually quite exquisite, but personally I am not great at appreciating art, so I just took a quick look and left.

Strolling Around the City Center

Then headed to the city center, passing by the square in front of Hallgrímskirkja again, which features the statue of the famous Icelandic explorer Leifur Eiríksson. A seagull perching on top of the great man’s statue head was kind of funny.

After that, ate a freshly baked croissant from a bakery on the street~

An orange kitty by the street~ Super cute~

When coming back in the afternoon, the kitty was still lying in the exact same spot, such a cozy life~

Also saw a tree full of pigeons by the roadside（

Also encountered a super lively, agile, and cute kitty by the street! Looking at the pattern, it looks like a Bengal cat!

A statue encountered while walking by the sea. Commemorating the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the US and Iceland. The US has been Iceland’s big daddy for a long time…

It was still gloomy by the sea, which is probably the norm for Iceland. Compared to yesterday, it feels like two completely different vibes.

Not many pedestrians on the streets. Not many tourists either.

Walked to Höfði House again. Under the cloudy sky, it even looks a bit eerie.

The location of Höfði House is wonderful, literally ocean view housing. Opening the window, you can see Mount Esja across the sea. Living in such a beautiful environment, no wonder it could nurture famous painters.

Wanted to eat lunch, so searched for nearby Chinese restaurants on Google Maps. Turned out one single Icelandic lamb skewer costs 600 Icelandic Krona (about 6.18 SGD). For this price in China I could buy more than ten skewers QAQ

Reykjavik City Hall

Having nothing to do, decided to walk over to Reykjavik City Hall (Ráðhús Reykjavíkur). Next to Tjörnin Lake outside the City Hall, there were lots of seagulls, pigeons, and ducks. The small houses in the distance are colorful, and although the weather was gloomy, it still had a unique charm.

There are also many statues outside City Hall. But my personal artistic taste is not high enough, some are hard for me to appreciate（

Inside City Hall there is not much to see, some travel guides, plus a large 3D map of Iceland.

The view by this lake is still very beautiful! In the distance you can even see the top of Hallgrímskirkja. There is also quite a lot of pretty greenery by the lake.

Also in Reykjavik you can often see planes flying super close to the ground, looking massive! Probably because Reykjavik Airport is right nearby.

Dinner

Today’s dinner was instant noodles bought at the supermarket for 60 Icelandic Krona… taste was very ordinary (after all it was just to fill the stomach). Of course cannot forget skyr! Today was pudding flavor~ but felt like it was not as tasty as the fruit flavors.

entry.title: 【Day 3】Iceland 5-Day Trip
entry.content:
Day 3 heading to the Golden Circle~

On the Way to the Bus Station

Going to the bus station in the morning to meet up with the tour guide. Saw a cute kitty on the way there~

Heading to the Icelandic Golden Circle

The first destination of the Golden Circle is Þingvellir National Park, which takes about 1 hour to drive from Reykjavik. The scenery along the way on the bus is also really nice too~

Þingvellir National Park

Arrived at the destination Þingvellir National Park~ It is a World Cultural Heritage site!
The tour guide said this is the only place in the world where you can visually see the rift valley at the boundary of the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates on land. The big rift is called Silfra.


The scenery at the visitor center opposite is not bad either, very Icelandic vibes (?)

Nordic style little houses paired with this natural landscape is just so aesthetic!

Next, heading over to the canyon side~

Waited a long time for this flag to be blown up by the wind.. there just wasn’t much wind that day.. a bit of a pity.

Lunch

Heading to the next destination in the Golden Circle~ Eating lunch first after arriving~

It tastes thicker and denser than regular yogurt, very nice! Kinda like lemon cake. The price is also okay, this small box is about 300 Icelandic Krona.


The Icelandic specialty black bread (Rúgbrauð) is very soft, eating it feels a bit like cake (?), wet and sticky. The taste is a little sour, and you can taste the grain flavor. This small box of salad dressing bought from the supermarket is super delicious, with lots of small shrimp inside. The price is also very affordable, only about 400 Icelandic Krona. The background is the water vapor of the Geysir geothermal area, eating lunch accompanied by this sulfur smell has a special flavor (?)

Geysir Geothermal Area

This area has lots of steam vents, hot springs and boiling mud pools.

The highlight of this area is the Strokkur geyser, which erupts every ten minutes or so, reaching a height of about 20 meters, and every time it is full of onlookers. Truly very spectacular! Because time was limited, I only saw 3 eruptions, had to leave without recording a perfect and complete eruption moment QAQ

Gullfoss Waterfall

The scenery on the way to Gullfoss Waterfall is also awesome!

You can see rainbows at Gullfoss Waterfall when the weather is good, alas it was cloudy all morning today. It didn’t photograph as spectacularly as it looks in person either, slightly disappointed. Feels like it still needs color grading and filters to look good wow.

Return Trip

On the way back, the tour guide took us to a nearby ranch to pet the horses~ Because Iceland is relatively cold, Icelandic horses are also on the shorter side, with longer hair.

Took a nap on the way back, and the sun came out when I woke up! Iceland with sunshine is indeed more beautiful!

The sunlight hit the small island across the sea, exceptionally beautiful! This island is called Viðey, and there are often boats heading there from the Reykjavik pier. But there didn’t seem to be any attractions on the island so I didn’t go explore. One relatively famous thing is the Imagine Peace Tower, which is a memorial tower for John Lennon and Yoko Ono.

Höfði House was built in 1909 and is the former residence of Icelandic poet Einar Benediktsson. It is most famous for being the location of the Reykjavik Summit in 1986 between US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev, which was an important step in ending the Cold War.

Dinner was bread + salad dressing + ham, the pudding flavored skyr felt just okay. A large tub is about 500 Icelandic Krona, the price is very affordable.

entry.title: 【Day 2】Iceland 5-Day Trip
entry.content:
Day 2 in Iceland~

Breakfast

Bought a cinnamon roll and a vanilla roll from Brauð & Co~ This bakery is super famous, some reviews say it’s the best cinnamon roll in the world (

Both the vanilla and cinnamon rolls were 830 ISK each, fresh from the oven~ I’m not a huge fan of cinnamon, so I picked the vanilla one. It is very soft! (Fuwa fuwa~) The first few bites were pretty good, just a little sweet (I’m not used to sweets). Halfway through, it just felt too sweet and rich. My friend said the same thing about the cinnamon roll.

On the Street

The street signs are so weird~ I thought it meant “No holding hands with children” ( ) After translating it, I found out it means “pedestrian street.”

The weather has been pretty bad these last two days, either drizzling or overcast. The whole city is covered in dark clouds, which dampened my mood too qwq
Also, it’s impossible to tell the time from the sky! Morning, noon, or night, it all looks the same…

Flea Market

Decided to check out the flea market in the city center~ It’s called Kolaportið, and it’s only open on weekends.

The tour guide said that both Iceland and Japan were encouraged to start whaling by daddy USA ()

There are a lot of horses in Iceland

The traditional Icelandic sweater (Lopapeysa) is made from the unspun wool of Icelandic sheep and has a distinctive circular pattern around the shoulders. They aren’t cheap here, about 150 euros for one.

The uncle was very enthusiastic, showing us fish-skin ties and all kinds of dried fish skins, including shark and salmon.

Icelandic Phallological Museum

Off to the Phallological Museum across from the flea market~ It’s the museum with the largest display of penises in the world~ Tickets are 3500 ISK, and they don’t have student discounts qwq

Inside the museum, there are tons of animal penis specimens. The descriptions include the animals’ mating habits, penis size, etc., very detailed.

Seaside

After coming out of the Phallological Museum, we went for a walk by the nearby seaside.

Strolling the City Center

Walked from the seaside to the city center and around the City Hall~

Rainbow Street

Checking out the shops here~

Dinner

For dinner, we went to Icelandic Street Food, which mainly sells specialty soups with bread. A bowl of soup + bread is 2500 ISK. If you get the soup in a special bread bowl, it’s 3000 ISK. The soup comes with unlimited refills!

You can refill any of the three soups. We ordered the lamb soup and the shellfish soup. My advice is to order the shellfish soup first; the staff will scoop up a lot of langoustines. After that, just refill with the lamb soup. If you ask for a shellfish soup refill, you won’t get many shrimp, mostly just broth qwq

No matter how many times you refill the lamb soup, they always give you plenty of ingredients, so it’s a better deal. The shellfish soup has a creamy taste, which is interesting~ The lamb soup has big chunks of lamb, potatoes, and carrots. It’s delicious! (I had five bowls)

In Iceland, where a single hot dog costs 830, this place is such amazing value! Highly recommend!!!

Stroll After Dinner

Hallgrímskirkja

There’s a massive pipe organ at the church entrance. Someone was playing it when we went in. This instrument looks incredibly difficult to learn; you have to use both your hands and feet.

entry.title: 【Day 1】Iceland 5-Day Trip
entry.content:
Off to visit Iceland~

Amsterdam Schiphol Airport

I never really thought Singapore Changi Airport was that good… until I saw Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. The airport is huge, but it feels a bit old, lacks clear signage, and it’s hard to tell the different zones apart. The corridors are also too narrow. When the electric carts come by, they take up the entire walkway. Pedestrians have to stop and stand to the side to let them pass. The restrooms are small and old, and one of the stall doors was broken.

They sell tulip bulbs at the airport, and quite a few varieties too. About 10 euros a pack.

Reykjavík Keflavík International Airport

The flight from Amsterdam to Reykjavík, Iceland takes about 3 hours and 20 minutes. After landing, there was no need to go through customs or get visas/IDs/passports checked (or stamped or anything), it was quite a surprise. Keflavík Airport isn’t big, but it’s modernly designed and the restrooms are very clean. What’s interesting is that you have to walk through a shopping area to get to the exit, kinda gives off that “tourist attraction gift shop” vibe (XD)

Booked the FlyBus from the airport to the city center~

The yellow-green stuff on the ground isn’t grass, but hundred-year-old moss (

A lot of places on the highway were under repair. It gave off a “poor infrastructure, out in the countryside” kind of feeling ( )

Reykjavík City

I’d barely taken two steps after getting off the bus and I already saw a cat!! So fluffy and super cute!!!!

Who would believe this photo was taken at 9 PM~ The sunset is really late in August~

If you walk down this street, you reach the sea. On the other side of the sea are… (not enemies!) Across the sea are mountains~ It’s Mt. Esja.

Keep walking up the shopping street and you’ll reach Iceland’s most famous church: Hallgrímskirkja.

Behind me is the famous rainbow shopping street(Skólavörðustígur) (the tourist street)~

Even though it’s past 9 PM, there are still quite a lot of people.

Dinner

Tried the hot dog that Bill Clinton ate: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur
Supposedly the best hot dog in all of Europe~

买的时候外面下着小雨，站在屋檐下吃完的。。。天气比较冷，热热的热狗很不错！里面还有炸洋葱碎。黄色的是芥末酱，棕色的是咸咸的酱汁（具体是什么吃不太出来）。听说热狗是羊肉做的噢！味道确实好，但价格有点小贵，830冰岛克朗一个。朋友评价说不如宜家热狗qwq（后来在Bonus超市里找到了同款热狗，五个600冰岛克朗左右。。。之后就自己做了）

It was drizzling when we bought it, so we stood under the eaves to finish it… The weather was pretty cold, so the hot hot dog was really nice! It also had fried onion bits inside. The yellow one is mustard, and the brown one is a savory sauce (couldn’t quite tell what it was). I heard the hot dogs are made of lamb! It really was delicious, but the price was a bit steep, 830 ISK for one. My friend commented that it’s not as good as an IKEA hot dog qwq (Later we found the same hot dogs in a Bónus supermarket, about 600 ISK for a pack of five… so we just made them ourselves after that)

A Stroll After Dinner

On the way back, there were very few people on Rainbow Street, so I got some good photos~

Later, we walked back near Hallgrímskirkja and took a couple more shots.

entry.title: Visiting Foodhallen
entry.content:
Fourth day~

Lunch

Boiled a pack of pork and chive frozen dumplings. On sale it was about €3 a pack. Taste was just… okay…

On the way out I saw the dorm cat! Its name is Simba~ so adorable~ ❤
Heard from my Dutch friend that Dutch people always call orange cats Simba, because they look like the lion Simba XD

Dinner

For dinner we were planning to check out Amsterdam’s food court, Foodhallen. Google reviews looked pretty good.

There are tons of stalls inside: crepes, sushi, Vietnamese spring rolls, ramen, burgers, burritos, etc.

I ordered Bitterballen from De Ballen Bar. It is a traditional Dutch fried meatball. 4 for €4.25.

The sauce taste a bit weird and there is mustard inside. Don’t really enjoy it personally :P

The meatballs were beef. Inside they were soft and a bit loose, so at first bite I thought they were undercooked (but that’s actually how those meatballs are). The filling had some spices (couldn’t tell exactly which) and I didn’t find them especially tasty.

I also ordered a burger from The Butcher. The patty was grilled over charcoal. It was fine, a little bland. Price was about €13.

Stroll after dinner

Saw some nice buildings on the way back.

Also saw a super cute cat in a residential area!!! It came up and rubbed both our legs!!! Loved it!!!!








Duck with dark eye circles next to the canal XD

And there were people kayaking in the canal.

entry.title: Continue exploring the city centre
entry.content:
Third day in Amsterdam~

Lunch

Reheated last night’s leftovers in the microwave and ate them with white bread and pickles.

Dinner

For dinner, we went to a highly rated Dutch restaurant. When I was looking up tips online a lot of travel blogs mentioned this place, really eager to try it~

The decor was really special: photos of mothers everywhere~

We ordered the Hollandse Rijsttafel / Dutch rice dish — basically a little bit of each classic dish.
There were three dishes in total: Stamppot (hotchpotch), Suddervlees, and Hachée. The latter two were both stewed beef.
I’m not sure what the spread on the bread was made from, but it was delicious!

The two stewed-beef dishes tasted similar, one had slightly smaller chunks of beef and was cooked until more fall-apart tender. The apple sauce was pretty sweet, with large chunks of apple. The pickled purple radish was sweet and delicious. There were roast potatoes, steamed potatoes, and mashed potatoes mixed with sauerkraut. As expected, I’m still not a big fan of sauerkraut ().

I heard the sausages were from HEMA. I can buy some and try making it myself later. My personal score: 7/10!

Strolling in the city

Very cute Mini cars that can go onto the bicycle paths

Really nice weather, took a few photos of the canal~

We passed by a gelato store and saw very interesting flavours!

I later asked a local Dutch friend, apparently “Smurf” flavor is quite popular in the Netherlands and kids especially love it. But it seems to be just a plain sweet flavor?

entry.title: Amsterdam Chinatown
entry.content:
A visit to the city center~

Albert Heijn

There are a few supermarkets next to my dorm. Found some very interesting stuff:

Chinatown

Went to the Chinatown in city centre and browsed a few Chinese supermarkets. The products are actually cheaper than regular supermarkets in Amsterdam.

Saw many interesting architecture. There is actually a Chinese temple right in the centre of the street!

Dinner

We ate our dinner at a Chinese restaurant in Chinatown. The vegetarian and meat dishes have similar prices, around €20.

Here, every dish ordered comes with a free bowl of rice… kind of weird.

The packaging even has a tutorial on how to use chopsticks! First time seeing that~

The three of us ordered two dishes: one vegetarian, one meat. The portions were pretty large. The veg was luohan zhai (Buddha’s delight), which seemed to have about 7–8 ingredients: bean sprouts, bamboo shoots, broccoli, stuff like that. The meat was a three-roast combo. We had some left overs and packed it to go. Personally it was pretty meh… I’m sure I’d cook better myself XD.
Score: 4.5/10…

Finally I took a few photos in the city center~ They came out quite nice~

entry.title: Reach Amsterdam
entry.content:
Reached the Netherlands~

Hostel

My dorm is right next to campus. The location’s pretty good, only a five-minute walk to the train station~
There’s also a supermarket nearby, just a five-minute bike ride away!

Bicycles

As soon as I got off the train I saw so many bicycles… Sasuga kingdom of bikes~

There’s a bike parking area next to the university library, packed wall-to-wall with bikes… It’s my first time seeing so many bicycles!

Dinner

The restaurant was recommended by a friend. It is a highly reviewes Japanese ramen restaurant in the city center.

I ordered the daily special signature ramen (forgot the exact name), and since the description said it was extremely spicy I went for it (). The price was about €18.70.

It’s a tonkotsu broth with red chili oil on top. I suspect they added Pixian doubanjiang (spicy fermented bean paste)… because I actually bit into a few of those soybeans you get in the bean paste, and the flavor was pretty similar. The noodles are Sapporo-style curly yellow noodles, topped with roasted chicken, a huge handful of coriander, pickled bamboo shoots, fried onions, a few stalks of bok choy and chunks of napa cabbage.

The bean paste, coriander, bok choy and napa cabbage give me this stitched-together Sino-Japanese vibe (?), which is kind of weird. And it wasn’t as spicy as I imagined.

My friend ordered a bowl of miso ramen, and halfway through thought it was insanely salty…

Considering that price, you could eat 1.5 bowls of ramen in Singapore or 3 bowls in Japan… so I’ll give it a 6/10…

The moment I stepped out of the ramen shop I smelled a really weird foul odor and realized the place next door was that legendary “coffee shop” (weed shop).
(I hightailed it.)

entry.title: Flying Over
entry.content:
Singapore –> Amsterdam

Flying with KLM (Royal Dutch Airlines).
I originally wanted to pick Qatar or Emirates — comfy and cheap. But when I was booking, Israel and Iran were causing trouble again… Singapore Airlines even cancelled flights to Dubai… so I went with the direct flight after all.
The flight time is great: it leaves Singapore at midnight and lands in the Netherlands 13 hours later in the morning (so I could sleep the whole way).
It sounded lovely in my head, but the plane isn’t that comfortable and I still couldn’t fall asleep, qwq
That’s life for a broke student…

Boarding

KLM’s signature color is blue~ I only learned from the description that it comes from Delft pottery produced in the Netherlands. But it kind of looks like Chinese blue-and-white porcelain…

I looked it up and it really is modeled on traditional Chinese porcelain…

Airplane meal

Dinner


For the first meal I could choose between fried rice + satay chicken or beef-and-tomato pasta. I’ll definitely go with the first one hehes.
The fried rice tasted okay — it even had tiny dried shrimp. But the portion was way too small QAQ.
The side was sweet-and-sour shredded radish mixed with rice vermicelli (?), kind of strange.
Dessert was a blueberry jam cake, a bit too sweet qwq

Breakfast


The second airplane meal was breakfast — there were no options this time. It was mini pancakes + a classic roll + fruit + yogurt.
The pancakes with the cream spread was really tasty, not too sweet~

Others

Saw the sunrise from the plane yeyyeyy!! I think it was when we were flying over Turkey! (I wasn’t in the window seat so my photos turned out awful, sorryz)
